findings.summary: The local sanitizable DOM shape duplicates the author-document sanitizer type model.
findings.consequence: The two sanitizer modules now have parallel handwritten DOM boundary types, so future linkedom API or sanitizer traversal changes must be kept consistent in two places even though the structural contract is the same.
findings.evidence: server/utils/sla-article.ts lines 33-54 define SanitizableAttribute, SanitizableParent, SanitizableNode, SanitizableElement, and ParsedSlaArticle. server/utils/author-document.ts lines 18-38 define the same structural sanitizer types with only the SLA module adding querySelectorAll to the parsed document/body use case.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared SanitizableAttribute, SanitizableParent, SanitizableNode, and base SanitizableElement shape into a small shared server utility type, then extend only the SLA-specific querySelectorAll requirement locally.
